title: Surface-priority button variants and interruptible commit flow
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Several product teams have reported inconsistent button behavior across surfaces when actions are cancellable or return long-running results. Current issues include: (1) spinners that obscure label text on small icon/compact variants, (2) disabled states that block optimistic cancellation flows, (3) token overrides that create color/contrast regressions in high-contrast and dark themes, and (4) lack of a consistent affordance pattern for interruptible commits (cancel/undo) across primary/secondary/ghost variants.

Goal: Define and deliver a consistent set of Surface-Priority button variants with explicit rules for loading, cancelable commits, and icon-only affordances. Outcomes should include updated token guidance, accessible spinner implementations, a small component surface audit, and a rollout plan that prevents regressions.

Deliverables:
- New visual spec for "surface-priority" variant mapping (primary / secondary / ghost / subtle) that clarifies when a surface uses elevation vs tint for emphasis.
- Loading affordance spec: introduce an "inline-slot" approach (spinner appears to left of label for compact/regular; overlays avoided on icon-only) and a cancelable spinner pattern for long-running actions.
- Accessibility rules: ARIA patterns, focus behavior on cancel, and motion reduction guidance.
- Token matrix: recommended semantic tokens for each variant in light/dark/high-contrast, color fallbacks when KMD token overrides exist.
- Design QA checklist and regression test cases for engineering.

Acceptance criteria (how we know it's done):
- Figma components updated for all variants and accessible examples added.
- Design PR reviewed and approved by platform PM and engineering owner.
- Token changes documented in the tokens spreadsheet with explicit fallback values.
- A/B rollout plan documented (start with console non-critical routes, monitor telemetry for click-through and error/cancel rates).

Success metrics:
- No visual regressions reported in first two weeks after rollout for monitored routes.
- Reduction in cancel-related support tickets for targeted flows by 60% in first month.
- Accessibility audit passes (contrast, focus behaviour, aria announcements) for sample routes.
